info.title: Private File Vault — Verify Progress
info.description:
Verifying a file against a cloud remote reads the whole file over the network before answering, and that synchronous call has been seen cancelled by its caller before it finishes. This channel is the fix: `POST /remotes/{id}/verify` (see api/openapi.json) starts answering `202` with a `job_id`, and everything past that point — progress, and the eventual match/mismatch/unknown — arrives here instead of in the response body.

The REST call stays authoritative for the job's existence. If the socket never connects, or drops mid-job, the job still ran; there is just nowhere left to hear how it ended. That is an accepted gap for now, not a design goal — see api/openapi.json's own note on why the socket is an accelerator for a progress bar, not a dependency.

Scoped to verify alone. `scan` and `ingest` (`POST /drives/{id}/scan`, `POST /drives/{id}/ingest`) have the same problem — both already answer `202` with nothing to poll or listen to — but they process many files, not one, so their progress almost certainly needs a different shape (a per-file list, not a single byte count) rather than a `kind` field bolted onto this message. That decision is deferred to when one of them is actually wired, not guessed at here.

Still open, deliberately not answered here: how Claude Design's mock-based preview (`api/interactions.json`, which records only request/response pairs) is supposed to represent a stream.

local.description: Single connection for the whole app. There is one user and no auth (see docs/roadmap.md's auth note), so the server broadcasts every verify job's messages to every open socket rather than scoping a connection to one job; a client filters to the `job_id` it started, client-side. Alongside `/api/...`, matching where the REST surface already lives.

verifyProgress.title: Verify progress
verifyProgress.description: Every message here is a `verify.progress` for a job started by `POST /remotes/{id}/verify`. A client tracks the job it cares about by the `job_id` that call's `202` response gave it, and ignores messages for any other id.

publishVerifyProgress.summary: The server sends one verify.progress per state change of a running verify job.
publishVerifyProgress.description: Sent zero or more times while `status` is `running`, then exactly once more in a terminal state (`complete` or `failed`). A client that opens the socket after a job has already finished simply never sees that job's terminal message — there is no replay.

VerifyProgress.description: One verify job's state as of `emitted_at`. The same shape whether it is still running or has finished, so a client has exactly one message to parse and one field — `status` — to check for "is this done yet".

emitted_at.description: When the server sent this message, not when the state it describes changed. Delivery order is not guaranteed across a reconnect; a client discards a message that arrives after a newer one for the same `job_id` rather than trusting arrival order.

error.description: Why the job failed, in a sentence worth showing verbatim. Present only when `status` is `failed`. A plain string, not a code: there is no branch in this UI that reacts differently to one failure reason versus another, only "show it, offer to retry".
examples: reading photos/2026/holiday.jpg on OpenDrive: connection reset by peer

job_id.description: Correlates this message to the `job_id` the triggering `202` response returned. Opaque beyond that — a client matches it, never parses it.

progress.description: Bytes hashed so far. Absent until the file has been stat'd and its size is known — render that as indeterminate, not as `0`.

result.description: The verification outcome. Present only when `status` is `complete` — the same information `POST /remotes/{id}/verify` returned synchronously before this channel existed (see `Verification` in api/openapi.json).

copies.description: How many other remotes have a copy of this file recorded.

hash.description: SHA-256 of the file as it is on this remote, computed by this job.

status.description: `match`: hashes agree. `mismatch`: a copy is recorded elsewhere but this remote's bytes disagree with it. `unknown`: no copy is recorded anywhere else, so nothing was compared and the file was never hashed — `hash`/`stored_hash`/`copies` are all absent in that case.

stored_hash.description: SHA-256 the database has on record for a copy on another remote. Differs from `hash` exactly when `status` is `mismatch`.

status.description: `running` covers the job from the moment the server accepted it, including before `progress`/`total` are known — there is no separate `queued` state, since nothing about this job is enqueued behind other work today. Exactly one of `complete` or `failed` is the last message a job ever sends.

total.description: The file's size in bytes. Absent exactly when `progress` is absent.
